name: T13-am-kill
description: Background, then kill the process 5s later.

steps.why: let the startup upload settle before backgrounding. This wait is load-bearing for TWO things and only one is obvious: the minimum-upload-interval floor (now unarmed at launch, so not the reason) AND letting the ~5s startup upload ACK before the app backgrounds. If it is still in flight it competes with the backgrounding upload and both die at the ~5s firewall cutoff. 18s covers typical ack latency (1.3-2s) and moderate outliers (8.5s observed); the tail reaches 23s, which no wait can cover, so parse_logs flags startup_upload_in_flight per run instead of pretending otherwise.

kill lands at ~ON_STOP+390ms, reliably BEFORE the ack. Bracketed on a Pixel 10: +390ms and +865ms both beat the ack, while +1.32s lost to a 974ms ack. Ack latency ranges 633-1535ms, so no wait reliably lands on the ack's side -- aim at the side that reliably tests something. This exercises the recovery path: the disk write survives (+25ms) and the snapshot is re-uploaded on next launch, verified by uuid.
long enough to see whether the snapshot is recovered on the next process start
